guide_q: why does a transaction pay change back to the person spending?
note: guide_q / agent / root: the questions the page test asks the guide and one agent, so that the test can check that the guide hands over to the right person. The Linkage agent covers the transaction chain, making change and coin selection; all three have executed examples, so the follow-up asking for an example can be answered, and with three concepts it is far from the largest agent (Mining has fourteen, the transaction-part agent thirteen). The switches say what SEN0401 does not yet have, so that the checks needing it are listed as skips instead of failures: corpus_kinds leaves out a textbook and a course ontology, and course_outcomes leaves out LO-n learning outcomes. code_layers is false: every worked example of this chapter is a single Python expression rather than a program of several statements, so the ontology graph draws only the meaning relations and no syntax or behaviour links (a full-page test run with the switch set to true reported sy=0 and be=0). The question bank is complete (an item for every one of the 101 concepts), so bank_complete is not set to false. The corpus_kinds switch now lists book as well: the page embeds the ontology of its own chapter of Mastering Bitcoin, 3rd edition (mastering-bitcoin-3e, at a pinned commit), so the agents really do rank over book passages and the check that counts the kinds must expect one. course_outcomes stays false until SEN0401's own course-level ontologies exist; when they do, the corpus gains a course kind too and this switch is bumped again.
